problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[1,32]\times [1,3]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)={x}^{3}+{y}^{3}-3{x}^{2}-3{y}^{2}+6.
$$

Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process for optimization that starts at ${x}_{0}=[1.5,\,1.5]^{T}$ if the first iteration of the algorithm gives ${x}_{1}=[2.25,\,2.25]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to **three decimal places.**

| ${x}_{2}=[$ | {{field-1}} | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-2}} |  |  |
worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}+{y}^{3}-3{x}^{2}-3{y}^{2}+6) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}+{y}^{3}-3{x}^{2}-3{y}^{2}+6)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-6x \\ 3{y}^{2}-6y\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{x}^{2}-6x) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(3{y}^{2}-6y) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}-6x) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(3{y}^{2}-6y)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6x-6 & 0 \\ 0 & 6y-6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}6x-6 & 0 \\ 0 & 6y-6\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-6x \\ 3{y}^{2}-6y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-{[\begin{aligned}6x-6 & 0 \\ 0 & 6y-6\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-6x \\ 3{y}^{2}-6y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2.25 \\ 2.25\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}6(2.25)-6 & 0 \\ 0 & 6(2.25)-6\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3(2.25)^{2}-6(2.25) \\ 3(2.25)^{2}-6(2.25)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2.25 \\ 2.25\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}7.5 & 0 \\ 0 & 7.5\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1.6875 \\ 1.6875\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2.25 \\ 2.25\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{7.5\cdot 7.5-0\cdot 0}[\begin{aligned}7.5 & 0 \\ 0 & 7.5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1.6875 \\ 1.6875\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2.25 \\ 2.25\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{56.25}[\begin{aligned}12.656\,25 \\ 12.656\,25\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2.025 \\ 2.025\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
